# Python project helpers


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

Utilities shared by Python project tooling (`nbdev`, `fastship`, and
friends): walking up to project files and locating package directories,
updating generated module variables via AST, and reading, writing, and
bumping `X.Y.Z` / `X.Y.Z.postN` versions.

``` python
from fastcore.test import *
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
```

### find_pyproject

``` python
def find_pyproject(
    start:str | pathlib.Path | None=None, # Starting directory or file (defaults to current working directory)
)->pathlib.Path:
```

*Find the nearest `pyproject.toml` in `start` or its parent directories*

[`find_pyproject`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/project.html#find_pyproject)
walks parent directories via
[`find_file_parents`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/xtras.html#find_file_parents),
and
[`is_uv_workspace`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/project.html#is_uv_workspace)
detects uv workspace roots:

``` python
_ws_td = TemporaryDirectory()
_ws = Path(_ws_td.name)
(_ws/'pyproject.toml').write_text('[tool.uv.workspace]\nmembers = ["*"]\n')
_proj = _ws/'my-pkg'
(_proj/'python'/'my_pkg').mkdir(parents=True)
(_proj/'python'/'my_pkg'/'__init__.py').write_text('')
(_proj/'pyproject.toml').write_text('[project]\nname = "my-pkg"\n[tool.maturin]\npython-source = "python"\n')
test_eq(find_pyproject(_proj/'python'), (_proj/'pyproject.toml').resolve())
assert is_uv_workspace((_ws/'pyproject.toml').read_toml())
```

### project_root

``` python
def project_root(
    path:str | pathlib.Path | None=None, # Starting path (defaults to current working directory)
)->tuple[pathlib.Path, dict, pathlib.Path | None]: # `(root, data, pyproject_path)`
```

*Nearest non-workspace project `(root, data, pyproject_path)`, falling
back to `(resolved_path, {}, None)`*

[`project_root`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/project.html#project_root)
skips uv workspace roots so member directories without a
`pyproject.toml` (such as pure Rust crates) resolve cleanly to
themselves:

``` python
_root,_data,_pp = project_root(_proj/'python')
test_eq((_root, _pp), (_proj.resolve(), (_proj/'pyproject.toml').resolve()))
_crate = _ws/'pure-crate'
_crate.mkdir()
test_eq(project_root(_crate), (_crate.resolve(), {}, None))
```

### find_pkg_path

``` python
def find_pkg_path(
    root:str | pathlib.Path, # Project root directory
    data:dict=None, # Parsed `pyproject.toml` dict (read from `root/pyproject.toml` if None)
    pkg:str=None, # Explicit package directory name override
)->pathlib.Path:
```

*Locate the Python package directory under `root` from `pyproject.toml`
config or standard layouts*

[`find_pkg_path`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/project.html#find_pkg_path)
checks `[tool.nbdev].lib_path`, maturin/setuptools source roots,
explicit `pkg` overrides, normalized `[project].name`, and standard
layouts:

``` python
test_eq(find_pkg_path(_root, _data), _root/'python'/'my_pkg')
test_eq(norm_mod('my-pkg'), 'my_pkg')
with expect_fail(FileNotFoundError): find_pkg_path(_crate, {})
_ws_td.cleanup()
```

### set_py_var

``` python
def set_py_var(
    path:str | pathlib.Path, # Python file to create or update
    name:str, # Top-level variable name to set or remove
    val, # Value to format with `pprint.pformat`, or `None` to remove
    *, header:str='# AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT!\n', # Header prepended when creating a missing file
    width:int=140, # Line width passed to `pprint.pformat`
    indent:int=2, # Indentation passed to `pprint.pformat`
    compact:bool=False, # Compact formatting passed to `pprint.pformat`
    top:bool=False, # Insert after shebang/coding/docstring instead of appending when absent?
)->bool: # True if file was created, updated, or unlinked
```

*Create, update, or remove a top-level `name = ...` assignment in `path`
via AST*

[`set_py_var`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/project.html#set_py_var)
creates, updates, and removes top-level assignments in place while
preserving sibling variables, unlinking autogenerated files when their
last variable is removed:

``` python
with TemporaryDirectory() as td:
    p = Path(td)/'_meta.py'
    assert set_py_var(p, 'a', {'k': 1}) and not set_py_var(p, 'a', {'k': 1})
    assert set_py_var(p, 'b', [1, 2]) and set_py_var(p, 'a', {'k': 2})
    test_eq(parse_py(p.read_text()).literals, {'a': {'k': 2}, 'b': [1, 2]})
    assert set_py_var(p, 'a', None) and parse_py(p.read_text()).literals == {'b': [1, 2]}
    assert set_py_var(p, 'b', None) and not p.exists() and not set_py_var(p, 'b', None)
```

### read_version

``` python
def read_version(
    path:str | pathlib.Path, # Package directory or `__init__.py` file
)->str | None:
```

*Read literal `__version__` from `path` (or `path/__init__.py`),
returning `None` if absent*

[`read_version`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/project.html#read_version)
extracts a literal `__version__` string from a package directory or
`.py` file, returning `None` when missing:

``` python
test_is(read_version(Path('nonexistent_pkg')), None)
```

<a

### set_version

``` python
def set_version(
    path:str | pathlib.Path, # Package directory or `__init__.py` file
    version:str, # New version string
)->bool: # True if file was created or updated
```

*Set literal `__version__` in `path` (or `path/__init__.py`), inserting
after shebang/coding/docstring when absent*

[`read_version`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/project.html#read_version) and
[`set_version`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/project.html#set_version)
accept either a package directory or a `.py` file;
[`set_version`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/project.html#set_version)
updates an existing `__version__` in place without adding extra blank
lines, or inserts it after any module docstring:

``` python
with TemporaryDirectory() as td:
    pkg = Path(td)/'demo'
    init = pkg/'__init__.py'
    init.mk_write('"Demo pkg."\n\nimport os\n')
    test_is(read_version(pkg), None)
    assert set_version(pkg, '0.1.0')
    test_eq(read_version(pkg), '0.1.0')
    test_eq(init.read_text(), '"Demo pkg."\n__version__ = "0.1.0"\n\nimport os\n')
    assert not set_version(init, '0.1.0') and set_version(init, '0.1.1')
    test_eq(init.read_text(), '"Demo pkg."\n__version__ = "0.1.1"\n\nimport os\n')
```

### bump_version

``` python
def bump_version(
    v:str, # Current version in `X.Y.Z` or `X.Y.Z.postN` format
    part:int=None, # Component to bump (`0`=major, `1`=minor, `2`=patch); default bumps `.postN` if present else patch
    unbump:bool=False, # Decrement instead of incrementing (clamped at 0)?
)->str:
```

*Bump `.postN` by default when present, else semver `part` (0=major,
1=minor, 2=patch)*

[`bump_version`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/project.html#bump_version)
accepts strict `X.Y.Z` and `X.Y.Z.postN` versions, defaulting to
`.postN` when present or patch otherwise:

``` python
test_eq([bump_version('1.2.3'), bump_version('1.2.3', 1), bump_version('1.2.3', 0)], ['1.2.4', '1.3.0', '2.0.0'])
test_eq(bump_version('0.0.0', unbump=True), '0.0.0')
test_eq([bump_version('2026.10.28.post0'), bump_version('2026.10.28.post2', unbump=True), bump_version('2026.10.28.post2', 2)],
    ['2026.10.28.post1', '2026.10.28.post1', '2026.10.29'])
with expect_fail(ValueError): bump_version('9.7.1.2')
with expect_fail(ValueError): bump_version('1.2.3', 3)
```
